race_context: The district: Perry Central Community School Corporation is based in Leopold in Perry County and runs Perry Central Elementary School and Perry Central Junior-Senior High School {nces_pc}{nces_pc_schools}. The high school was formed in 1962 by merging the Leopold, Oil Township and Tobinsport high schools {wiki_pchs}. Federal data list 1,275 students {nces_pc}. Dr. Tara Bishop is superintendent {wfie_award}{pc_award}.

Board officers elected January 12, 2026: Tim Edwards (president), Glenn Etienne (vice president), Kevin Etienne (secretary) and Nan DuPont (assistant secretary) {pc_reorg}. This guide could not confirm the full size of the board or how its district seats are drawn.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the state list shows two races, District 1 and District 2, each electing one member {in_list}. Glenn M Etienne, the board's vice president, is unopposed in District 2, and Nanette L DuPont, a current board member, faces Scott D Peter in District 1 {in_list}{pc_reorg}. This guide could not confirm from an official source which district seat each incumbent holds now.

Recognition (November–December 2025): Perry Central was the only Indiana school corporation to receive the Department of Education's 2025 Hoosier Education Excellence Award, which carries a $50,000 grant, for its approach to literacy, STEM and college and career preparation {wfie_award}{pc_award}.
Teacher pay (November 2025): the board approved a new contract with the Perry Central Classroom Teachers Association giving all returning teachers a $2,000 base raise {pc_contract}.

Budget and programs (April 2026): the board discussed a new plan to fund its after-school program after a delay in the federal 21st Century grant cycle left no grant money for 2026–27 {pc_afterschool}.

Special education (May–July 2026): a parent's advocate and then the parent raised concerns at board meetings about special education practices after an April incident involving the school's 'calming room' {pc_sped}{pc_sped_jul}.

Transportation: in February 2026 the board heard a presentation on propane school buses, and in September 2026 it introduced a policy requiring visual verification when students in preschool through third grade are dropped off {pc_propane}{pc_transport}.
This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Perry Central's budget, and no candidate forum or questionnaire for this race as of October 10, 2026.
